PullRequest.Title: Enhance Mac keyboard mapping with layout-dependent accelerators
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328194

## Summary

Display representable layout-dependent Mac shortcuts in the native menu accelerator column instead of appending the shortcut in brackets to the menu label. The captured European Portuguese layout (`com.apple.keylayout.Portuguese`, not Brazilian-Pro) produces `+` on physical Equal without Shift.

The revision deliberately keeps this fallback narrow:

- Add an explicit menu/global-shortcut purpose to the existing resolved-keybinding accelerator API. Native menu and context-menu consumers retain the menu default; both global-shortcut consumers request the conservative global purpose.
- Allow the new fallback only for unshifted, single printable ASCII base characters on Mac. Preserve existing stable/immutable mappings, Windows/US behavior, Linux punctuation restrictions, and shared chord/modifier/numpad exclusions.
- Keep newly eligible shifted, dead-key, uppercase, multi-character and non-ASCII/CJK cases on the existing fallback. Do not reuse the internal CJK-to-ASCII redirect for native menu matching.
- Preserve physical dispatch and user-settings labels. In particular, Portuguese `cmd+[Equal]` can display as `Cmd+Plus` in a menu but remains unsupported globally: Electron parses named Plus with implicit Shift, which does not preserve the original physical global shortcut.

Native testing also found that the original new `Shift+Cmd+'` Swiss fallback matches the unshifted event, not the intended shifted event. This revision rejects that new Shift fallback instead of inventing a modifier transformation.

## Testing

- Actual installed European Portuguese mapping captured read-only with TIS/UCKeyTranslate, following native-keymap's translation and dead-key conventions, on macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), keyboard type 40. Added the captured JSON fixture and provenance.
- **154 passing** in the real Electron 43.8.3 unit runner: Mac/Linux mapper snapshots and regressions, Windows mapper, shared keybinding labels, and system-wide selection (including rejected-first ordering, arguments/context and duplicates).
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`, `npm run typecheck-client`, targeted hygiene/ESLint, module-layer checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Real AppKit `NSMenu.performKeyEquivalent` tests with per-modifier captured `NSEvent` character fields: Portuguese Command-plus, Option-Command-plus and corrected Swiss unshifted apostrophe each invoke once for the intended event and reject the other eleven sampled combinations.
- Actual compiled baseline/revised mappers fed an Electron 43.8.3 native menu/context-menu harness. Owned-window capture confirms the baseline `Zoom In [⌘+]` inline label versus the revised right-hand `⌘+` accelerator.

### Coverage boundaries

The layout capture did not select/change the user's active input source. Native event matching used synthesized captured-layout events; the Electron visual check used a dedicated harness, not a full VS Code workbench run. Physical European Portuguese hardware and a full-workbench end-to-end keystroke run remain manual coverage, not claimed here. The implicit-Shift global-registration incompatibility is source/data-flow evidence; the revision prevents admission instead of registering an OS-wide shortcut.

The original contribution is preserved, with main merged without rewriting contributor history. Keyboard-owner review remains requested from alexdima.

Scenarios.Scenario: macOS native menubar construction and refresh on menu/keybinding changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The focused renderer walks the current menu tree, resolves one accelerator per bound action, serializes the complete menubar payload, and sends one updateMenubar IPC before the native menu reflects the refresh. The diff adds only a bounded fallback after the existing immutable/stable-key checks for previously unsupported Mac scan codes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the complete menubar model to the Electron main process for native rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped IPC call per accepted menubar rebuild, regardless of menu item count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped updateMenubar IPC was sent; unsupported layout-dependent shortcuts used a non-native label rather than a native accelerator field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Native menu refresh waits on construction and dispatch of this existing payload; accelerator fallback adds constant local lookups but no extra IPC call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total menu actions with keybindings; the added branch executes only for layout-dependent scan codes that failed the existing stable-key lookup, so effective cardinality is at most the number of bound menu items in one rebuild.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Menu traversal and accelerator formatting are synchronous and serial. The full tree is grouped into one existing asynchronous menubar IPC update; the diff adds no queue, task, or parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The keyboard mapper and its precomputed scan-code tables are reused for both cold and warm menu rebuilds. The new two-entry named-character map is module-scoped; there is no per-item retained cache, miss retry, or invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch and complete consumer path are directly traced; only constant-time property checks, character checks, and a two-entry Map lookup are added after existing resolution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact menu size and rebuild frequency vary by installed contributions, but the added CPU is constant per affected binding and introduces no boundary or collection-wide nested work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Work remains O(menu items), with a small bounded increment only for previously unsupported Mac layout-dependent bindings and unchanged IPC cardinality.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: On each native context-menu invocation, the renderer recursively maps visible actions to serializable items, resolves an accelerator for each bound action, then sends the full menu in one synchronous ipcRenderer.send. The added mapper fallback is on this pre-popup critical path only for unstable Mac scan codes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and send one native context-menu payload to the Electron main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one IPC send per shown native context menu, with all actions grouped into that message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same menu and item were serialized in the same single IPC payload; unsupported accelerators caused the already-computed keybinding label to be appended to the item label.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC remains on the popup critical path. The diff can change an item's serialized accelerator value but does not add messages or increase item cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible context-menu actions and submenu actions; effective added work is one constant-time fallback for each bound action whose scan code is neither immutable nor stable.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Menu item creation is synchronous and serial, followed by one existing renderer-to-main IPC send. No fan-out or new concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved mapper tables are warm process state; no new per-menu cache exists or is needed because each fallback consists of bounded local reads. Cold and warm calls have the same asymptotic behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: createMenuItem calls the changed API once per bound action and popup groups all items into the unchanged single IPC boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Context-menu sizes and invocation frequency vary, but the fallback has no I/O, layout read, cache growth, or nested scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The synchronous path receives bounded constant work and the expensive native-menu boundary remains one call per popup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser View window-configuration synchronization after keybinding or configuration updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration generation resolves accelerators for a fixed list of three Browser View commands, packages them with the existing window configuration, and performs one browser-view service IPC. This path is asynchronous and the caller does not block startup on its promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the full per-window Browser View configuration to the main-process service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing IPC call per triggering configuration/keybinding event, containing all three relevant keybindings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full configuration IPC occurred with the same fixed three lookups; an unstable layout-dependent binding could be omitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The update is fire-and-forget from event handlers; the diff changes only a possible accelerator string in the existing payload.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed cardinality of three command IDs, independent of total keybindings or browser-view count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each event starts the existing full configuration update; accelerator resolution is serial over three commands and one service IPC follows. The diff neither adds update events nor changes concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No accelerator cache is used, but cardinality is fixed and mapper state is reused. Existing configuration updates behave the same on cold and warm paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the command array has three entries and all are grouped into the pre-existing service call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Event frequency depends on user configuration activity, but the diff adds no trigger and the local cardinality is statically bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Neither boundary count nor scaling changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: System-wide shortcut selection and synchronization after restore or keybinding/layout changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selector scans resolved keybindings, calls accelerator resolution only for user entries marked systemWide, then existing synchronizers debounce ordinary updates for 200 ms, serialize them through a Sequencer, skip structurally unchanged successful payloads, and send one grouped native-host IPC. The Agents owner performs its existing immediate initial sync.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize the grouped system-wide keybinding payload with the Electron main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one grouped call per coalesced update per existing owner, and zero for unchanged successful payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped synchronization ran, but default menu-purpose formatting could admit a layout-dependent accelerator into the existing payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The contribution runs after restore; ordinary updates are debounced and sequenced. Selecting globalShortcut purpose may remove unsupported menu-only entries but cannot add IPC calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register or unregister accepted accelerator strings with Electron globalShortcut in the main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration operation per deduplicated accepted accelerator in a changed payload; the diff can only exclude newly distinguished menu-only accelerators.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A layout-dependent accelerator could proceed to registration; the new purpose check returns null for it, reducing or preserving downstream cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registration is downstream of the existing asynchronous IPC and after-restored contribution, not on interactive menu rendering or startup restoration progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total resolved keybindings for the filter scan, with accelerator formatting limited to the effective number of user system-wide entries; duplicate accelerators are coalesced before IPC.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selection is synchronous. Standard updates are coalesced by one RunOnceScheduler and all syncs are serialized by one Sequencer; each owner has at most one in-flight sync. The changed globalShortcut purpose does not add work or concurrency and can reject a menu-only candidate earlier.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful payloads are structurally cached and skipped when unchanged; failed registrations remain retryable. The diff preserves these positive/failure behaviors and adds no cache key or retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: filter ordering, 200 ms coalescing, Sequencer serialization, structural payload cache, and grouped IPC are directly visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may configure few or many system-wide bindings, but effective downstream cardinality is deduplicated and the changed branch does not increase it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed purpose preserves local scan complexity and can reduce unsupported IPC payload/registration work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and every diff page. Runtime changes add only bounded local accelerator classification for previously unsupported macOS layout-dependent keys, while native menu, Browser View, and global-shortcut boundary cardinality, batching, scheduling, and cache lifecycles remain unchanged. Test-only JSON parsing adds one fixture read/parse per targeted test setup and is absent from product paths. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression or evidenced shipped performance-regression fix was found.
